_comment: Manual data file. Copy to data/network.json to use it.
Every top-level key is optional — supply only what no connector can reach yet.
Money is in whole CENTS. States are USPS two-letter codes.
Set "demo": false once these are real numbers; the demo banner keys off it.
_consumers_comment: `purchasers` is keyed by trailing window in days, plus "ever" for all-time.
The dashboard's time range picks the matching window. Send only the ones
you actually compute — a purchaser count can't be derived from a
neighbouring window, so any you omit report themselves as untracked
rather than borrowing another period's number.
The older purchased30d / purchased180d fields still work.
_gmv_comment: Gross merchandise value — what shoppers spent on our customers'
storefronts. This is NOT our revenue; we take a fee on it, so GMV runs an
order of magnitude larger. It cannot be derived from our revenue without
assuming a take rate, so it has to come from whatever processed the orders.
`gmv` is monthly; `gmvDaily` is optional and only needed if you want the
1W / 1M ranges to show GMV — without it those ranges report it untracked
_cash_comment: Cash on hand. A bank balance — it is NOT derived from revenue or MRR, and
it does not move with the dashboard's time range. List one entry per
account; the tile sums them and shows the OLDEST asOf date, since the total
is only as current as its stalest part.
Stripe can supply its own balance automatically; your operating account
has to come from here or the admin API.
_revenueDaily_comment: Optional. Powers the 1W and 1M ranges on the revenue chart.
Only include it if you genuinely have day-level figures — the dashboard
will not split monthly totals into days, and says so instead.
Stripe supplies this automatically; you rarely need it here.
